# booklens

> Offline EPUB accessibility audit and repair.

booklens audits an EPUB against EPUB Accessibility 1.1 and WCAG 2.x and writes a repaired EPUB back. It fixes metadata, language, headings, image alt text, and the navigation document, and reports what it cannot safely change. It also ships a typed library and a browser playground that audits real EPUB bytes.

It runs entirely offline, with no network calls and no telemetry. Output is human-readable text, stable JSON (one object for a single input, an array for many), SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning, and a corrected EPUB. Exit codes are `0` (no findings at or above `--fail-on`), `1` (findings), `2` (invalid usage or a file that cannot be parsed as an EPUB), and `3` (I/O error).

## Docs
- [Overview](https://srivtx.github.io/booklens/): Audit an EPUB and get a repaired book back, with an in-browser playground.
- [Rules](https://srivtx.github.io/booklens/rules): The fifteen rules, how an EPUB is audited, and what `fix` changes.
- [Usage](https://srivtx.github.io/booklens/usage): CLI flags, exit codes, JSON output, and the TypeScript library API.
- [CI](https://srivtx.github.io/booklens/ci): SARIF 2.1.0 output for GitHub code scanning and an exit-code gate for pull requests.
- [FAQ](https://srivtx.github.io/booklens/faq): Scope, limitations, and comparisons to DAISY ACE, EPUBCheck, and Access-Aide.

## Optional
- [Source](https://github.com/srivtx/booklens): TypeScript implementation, tests, and issue tracker.
- [Install script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/srivtx/booklens/main/install.sh): One-line install of the `booklens` binary.
